title: Lambdas, higher-order functions and the trailing lambda

videos.script: Count the long sessions. Then the short ones. Then the ones on a weekend. Three loops, identical except for one line. {{types}} This lesson makes that one line a value. A function you can store, pass, and return, with a type of its own. {{lambda}} A lambda is a function written in braces, with no name. You will learn the four rules that cover almost every one you read, and why return inside one is refused. {{higher}} Then a function that takes another function. The loop is written once, and the question becomes an argument. {{trailing}} The trailing lambda. One rule about where the braces go, and it is why repeat looks like part of the language, and why a Compose screen looks the way it does. {{closures}} What a lambda remembers about the variables around it. {{inline}} And inline, which copies a lambda into its caller, so it costs nothing, and lets return leave the outer function.
